### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b177920076f7fd27ac6d0b6717d56f0db04b64f4`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b177920076f7fd27ac6d0b6717d56f0db04b64f4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f94618dae89a6be7348a777b6230f4c9c2af3f15` — the merge of head `1ee7e4f58fcb24aeeb60f3290f423ee6d545e8e0` into base `b177920076f7fd27ac6d0b6717d56f0db04b64f4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f94618dae89a6be7348a777b6230f4c9c2af3f15 && git checkout f94618dae89a6be7348a777b6230f4c9c2af3f15
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b177920076f7fd27ac6d0b6717d56f0db04b64f4 1ee7e4f58fcb24aeeb60f3290f423ee6d545e8e0 && git checkout -B drift-repro b177920076f7fd27ac6d0b6717d56f0db04b64f4 && git merge --no-ff 1ee7e4f58fcb24aeeb60f3290f423ee6d545e8e0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b177920076f7fd27ac6d0b6717d56f0db04b64f4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b177920076f7fd27ac6d0b6717d56f0db04b64f4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1ee7e4f58fcb24aeeb60f3290f423ee6d545e8e0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-collection-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-app-publish-gate.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-query-arity-doors.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/dispatcher-query-arity.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-list-projection-parity.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/meta-read-doors-live.dogfood.test.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts (the dispatcher's `/meta` branches: `metaQueryArityRefusal('list' | 'book-tree' | 'drafts' | 'state')`, `metaItemQueryRefusal('item' | 'layers' | 'published' | 'save')`, the `packageBinding` closure, the `rule !== 'layered-member'` reader), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`metaItemPackageBinding`, `serveMetaItemLayered`, `META_ITEM_RESET_PARAMS`, `META_ITEM_PUBLISH_PARAMS`), packages/rest/src/meta-item-write-routes.ts and packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts (the write, publish and `/published` doors' `refuseUnknownQueryParams` sets), packages/rest/src/meta-collection-routes.ts (the diagnostics and `_drafts` doors beside the list), packages/rest/src/index.ts and packages/rest/package.json (the `exports` map and the entry's export list), packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts (`readDispatchQuery`), packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts (`readQuery`), packages/client/src/index.ts (the `?package=` / `?object=` builders), `ui/**` (read only, for the producer census), .changeset/29199-bracketed-object-package-refused.md (read for ②), PR #29046's contract review record 6570942095 and the rest CHANGELOG entries for #23072 and #23214 (precedent for ②). Inputs: card #29199 body and its four comments (triage 6574247482, claim 6574465942, os-dev-report 6575874431, claim amendment 6575888036), PR #29298 body, file list and net diff against `origin/main` at this head, and the check-runs on this head. The merge-base and the branch were read with `git show` / `git grep` on fetched refs; nothing was built, run, re-run or ablated here. No `reviewFace` path hit: `record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths <file list>` reports no schema or governed path and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line, so the narrowing face is the one owed and the scope floor is every path outside the prose faces; all eight are listed above.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each read against the cited code on `origin/main` and on the head:

1. **`GET /meta/view` and `GET /meta/views` with any query key that opens `object[` (`?object[]=NAME`, `?object[0]=NAME`, `?object[name]=NAME`): 200 with every view the caller may see → 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, no list, on both transports.** Right. Both adapters still build the query with `Object.fromEntries` over `c.req.queries()` and parse no brackets (`readQuery`, `readDispatchQuery`), so the key reaches the chain spelled as sent; the list door declares no closed set and `META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS.list` names `object`, not `object[`, so neither entry gate catches it; on the merge-base step 4 read `query?.object` only and the key fell through to the unfiltered list, which is the card's measurement. On the head step 4 asks `refuseBracketedListFilter(query, 'object', 'object', 'view')` before `query?.object` is read, keyed on the folded `metaType === 'view'` (`metaTypeSingular` on the REST route, `pluralToSingular` in the dispatcher's list branch at `meta.ts` ~2174), so `views` is covered and pinned. The throw is `throwListFilterRefusal`'s `Error` with `status = 400`, `code = 'VALIDATION_ERROR'`, the shape #28548 and #29046 already traced through `handleRouteError` (REST, flat `{ error, code }`) and `answerMetaList`'s `errorFromThrown` (dispatcher). Pinned: the rest unit (three keys × three caller postures × two spellings, full sentence, no `items`, no bare array), the dispatcher arity test (`object[]` on the dispatcher's `/meta/view`), the parity census (`?object[]=lead`, `?object[0]=lead` on every type × caller, both transports) and its reference row, and the dogfood over HTTP as admin and as a member.
2. **`GET /meta/:type` (every list type) and `GET /meta/book/:name/tree` with any query key that opens `package[`: 200 across every package → 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` on both transports.** Right. `metaBracketedPackageRefusal(door, query)` answers only where `META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS[door]` names `package` (`list` and `book-tree`; `drafts` and `state` return `undefined`, pinned). `RestServer`'s list door (`meta-collection-routes.ts` 644-651) and tree door (`meta-item-read-routes.ts` 388-395) ask it right after `refuseRepeatedQueryParams` and before `metaItemPackageBinding(req.query?.package)`, and write it in the nested `{ error: { code, message } }` their arity gate writes; the dispatcher's list (`meta.ts` 2174) and tree (1149) get it through `metaQueryArityRefusal`, which now returns `repeatedOnceRefusal(...) ?? metaBracketedPackageRefusal(...)`, so no runtime source moved. The dev's premise that `metaItemPackageBinding(raw)` cannot see the key is right: it receives the VALUE of `query.package` (`rest-server.ts` 1854, `typeof raw === 'string' && raw !== '' && raw !== 'all' ? raw : undefined`), which is `undefined` for a bracketed key, so "the binding's one seam" in the order could not be taken literally and the arity decision is the one seam both transports ask before any read of `package`. Pinned on both transports and over HTTP (`/meta/object?package[]=`, `?package[0]=`), with `getMetaItems` asserted never called on `RestServer`.
3. **Rule order and multiplicity: a repeated plain `package` still answers the multiplicity sentence first; a bracketed key beside a plain one is refused (two spellings of one filter/scope); a bracketed key sent twice arrives as an array under `package[]`, which `repeatedOnceRefusal` never reads (it iterates the door's named keys only), so the bracket arm answers it with one sentence.** Right, read in `repeatedOnceRefusal` and `bracketedKeyOf`; the first two are pinned.
4. **#29046's and #28548's answers are byte-identical.** Right. `listFilterRefusalMessage(key, names, got, notAFilter, 'list', \`list every ${lists} you can see\`)` expands to exactly the merge-base literal of `throwListFilterRefusal` (`Query parameter '${key}' names no ${names}; ${got}. The list was not served: ${notAFilter} is not a filter. Name one ${names}, or leave the parameter out to list every ${lists} you can see.`); the `id` arm's `got` and `notAFilter` templates with `param = 'id'`, `names = 'app'` expand to `the 'id' filter takes exactly one app name, spelled ?id=NAME` and `a bracketed 'id' key`, the merge-base literals; `refuseEmptyListFilter` is untouched. Every hunk in the five test files is an addition, so #29046's `id[…]` pins and #28548's empty-value pins run unchanged on this head.
5. **Everything else is unchanged.** Right, read in the diff and the cited code: `?object=NAME` still switches and an absent `object` lists all (controls pinned); a bracketed `object` key on any type but `view` stays unread, as `?object=` is there (rest control on `app`, the census's 2 probes × every type); `packages[`, `packageId` and `ID[` do not match `startsWith('package[')` / `startsWith('object[')`; a non-object query returns early from `bracketedKeyOf`; `?package=ID` scopes, `?package=all` and no `package` read every package (controls pinned); the `/data` filter slot and every non-`/meta` door are untouched.
6. **No write door's behaviour changes, and every other `/meta` door that reads `package` already refuses `package[` as an unknown name, on both transports.** Right, read door by door on the head: `RestServer` item read (`metaItemQueryRefusal('item')` at `meta-item-read-routes.ts` 461, closed set `META_ITEM_QUERY_DOORS.item.accepted` names `package` not `package[`), `/layers` (`metaItemQueryRefusal('layers')` at 323 before `serveMetaItemLayered`'s binding read at `rest-server.ts` 4322), `/published` (`refuseUnknownQueryParams(META_ITEM_PUBLISHED_PARAMS)`, history-routes 1143), `PUT` (`refuseUnknownQueryParams(META_ITEM_SAVE_PARAMS)`, write-routes 281), `DELETE` (`META_ITEM_RESET_PARAMS`, 482), `POST …/publish` (`META_ITEM_PUBLISH_PARAMS`, history-routes 666), `/meta/diagnostics` (`unknownQueryParamRefusalMessage(req.query, META_DIAGNOSTICS_PARAMS)`, collection-routes 337); the dispatcher's item (`meta.ts` 1737), `/layers` (1193), `/published` (1239) and `PUT` (1519) each ask `metaItemQueryRefusal` before the `packageBinding()` read, and the dispatcher serves no `DELETE`, `/publish` or diagnostics twin (read in `meta.ts`). The dev's measured table matches the tree; the order's "stop if it reaches a WRITE door" condition was not met.
7. **Public surface.** `metaBracketedPackageRefusal`, `refuseBracketedListFilter`, `bracketedKeyOf` and `listFilterRefusalMessage` are not on `packages/rest/src/index.ts`, and the package's `exports` map has the one `.` entry, so none is published. No new export, error code, status, answer member or wire field. The ONE published-face movement is the `rule` union of `MetaItemQueryRefusal`: the interface is not in the entry's `export type` list, but it is the declared return type of the exported `metaQueryArityRefusal` and `metaItemQueryRefusal`, so it is reachable from the entry type graph (the runtime already types against it as `ReturnType<typeof metaItemQueryRefusal>`), and its `rule` discriminator now carries a fourth member, `'bracketed-parameter'`. Judged under ② and ③.

Claims checked for wrong statements about the surface: the changeset's two "Now" sentences are the literals the builder and the tests pin; the PR body's door table holds against item 6; "no runtime source changed" holds (the runtime diff is two test files); "rest-server.ts untouched" holds. None found wrong.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29199-bracketed-object-package-refused.md`: `'@objectstack/rest': patch`; line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; a **BREAKING** banner; exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker; Before / Now / Unchanged / Who-sees-it; the remedy as FROM `?object[]=NAME` TO `?object=NAME` and FROM `?package[]=ID` TO `?package=ID`. The PR title carries `!`, and the PR body carries the same two declaration lines line-initial. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: `(narrowing)` is the BREAKING arm, and a non-protocol change ships `patch` with its banner and ADR-0087 disposition (ruling A, #25105, as #29046's record applied it). The level matches what the diff publishes: only `@objectstack/rest` ships changed source; `@objectstack/runtime` moves two test files its package does not ship; `packages/qa/dogfood` is private; nothing under `packages/spec` moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: a query-key spelling on a REST door changes nothing a metadata author writes. `Skills-docs: none` holds: `git grep` on the head finds no page under `skills/`, `content/docs/` or `apps/docs/` that spells `object[]` / `package[]` as a query key (the hits are TypeScript type notation in generated reference tables). `Check Changeset` and `Lint · repo & tooling gates` are green on this head.

**The `rule` member and the declaration line (the dev's open question).** The dev asks whether `'bracketed-parameter'` on `MetaItemQueryRefusal.rule` is a published widening and recommends A (keep it, keep `no (narrowing)`). My reading: the published face is the `exports` map's reachable type graph (contract-review.md), and ① item 7 shows the union is reachable, so the TYPE a consumer receives from an exported function is one member wider; a consumer that switches exhaustively on `rule` fails to compile against this head, which is the textbook sense in which an output union widening is a change. It is NOT a widening of any accept set (no door accepts more; every move is a refusal), no transport writes `rule` to the wire, and the only readers in the tree are the two `rule !== 'layered-member'` inequalities. The precedent on this same record spelled it the other way: #23072 (which introduced `MetaItemQueryRefusal` and `rule`) and #23214 (which introduced `metaQueryArityRefusal`) both shipped as `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with the same `patch` + BREAKING + ADR-0087 frame. So the exact spelling for "a published type grows AND an accept set narrows" is `yes (narrowing)`, option B, and A under-declares by one word. What the line protects is unchanged either way: both spellings owe this review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` with ④ (`reviewFace` maps `yes (narrowing)` to the narrowing face too), `check-adr-0087-registration` reads the arm and the kind, the level is `patch` under both, the banner and marker are present, and the changeset's own prose already names the widened tag in the open. Option C is wrong on the merits: `package[]` is a recognised key with a dedicated remedy, and tagging it `unknown-parameter` would misdescribe it to the one place `rule` is meant for (a transport that answers the third rule elsewhere). **Judged: should-fix, not must-fix** — respell `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` in the PR body and the changeset if this PR cuts another head for any reason; the under-declaration hides nothing, moves no gate, tier or level, and does not block landing on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions[0]` (the `rule` union, options A/B/C):** answered under ② — B is the precise spelling, A is accepted on this head as a should-fix, C is refused. Not escalated: no maintainer ruling is needed for a declaration spelling whose gate reading is identical.
- **Deviation: file surface (`rest-server.ts` named, `meta-collection-routes.ts` + `meta-item-read-routes.ts` touched instead).** Verified in the tree and accepted by the seat's claim amendment 6575888036 before this review; ① item 2 confirms the binding cannot see the key, so the arity decision is the seam the order's "at the binding's one seam" could only mean. Closed.
- **Deviation: runtime test files gained pins with no runtime source change.** Verified: the runtime diff is `dispatcher-query-arity.test.ts` (+32) and `meta-list-projection-parity.test.ts` (+16), additions only. Closed.
- **Deviation: dogfood red-first read off the ablation legs, not a main run of the dogfood file.** Coherent: each ablation arm restores main's code for that arm, and the two dogfood reds per arm are exactly that arm's two HTTP pins. Not re-run here (read-only). Accepted.
- **Deviation: `origin/main` moved 22 commits after the merge, none on a file this PR edits.** The queue's merge-group run is the check of record for that; nothing for this record.
- **Evidence: ablation.** Not re-run here. Read for coherence: the object arm reds exactly the three `object[…]` rows, the dispatcher `object[]` case, the reference row and the two dogfood view pins; the package arm reds exactly the ten bracketed-`package` rows, the four dispatcher list/tree cases, the reference row and the two dogfood object pins; the census rows staying green under ablation is the correct expectation (both transports then give the same unfiltered answer). Coherent with the diff. Accepted.
- **Evidence: the full dogfood battery.** `(narrowing)` owes it; reported under the verify lock at this head as 389 files passed, 3 skipped, 3220 tests passed, 28 skipped, no failures. The CI twin `Dogfood Regression Gate` is green on this head. Accepted.
- **Evidence: derived gates.** The dev's local record says 64 of 64 families run and green with three prerequisite re-runs declared. The verdicts of record are the head's check-runs, read from the API after the last one completed: 49 of 49 completed, 36 success and 13 skipped, none failed — including all eight `Test Core` shards, the four `Type Check` jobs, every `Lint` job, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Build Core`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI` and `Dogfood Regression Gate`. The skipped ones are opt-in harnesses, UI-matrix placeholders and the schedule gate. No merge-base comparison is needed, since nothing is red. The dev's report said CI was in progress at report time; it is green now.
- **Out-of-scope finding: `GET /meta/_drafts` `?packageId[]=` / `?type[]=`.** Verified in the tree as the same class: both transports read `req.query?.packageId` / `query?.packageId` and `type` after `refuseRepeatedQueryParams` / `metaQueryArityRefusal('drafts')` only, with no closed set (`META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS.drafts = ['packageId', 'type']`), so a bracketed key is unread and the draft list is answered across every package / every type. Unmeasured, outside the card's keys, and the order did not pull it in; it is a separate card, not a FAIL of this one. Recorded for that card: the fix is `metaBracketedPackageRefusal`'s shape generalised to the door's own names (`packageId`, `type`), asked at the same two call sites (`meta-collection-routes.ts` ~467 and `meta.ts` ~2067); `?preview[]=` and `?include[]=` on the list are the same adapter pass-through but read as "absent switch", a narrower consequence.
- **Precedent carried:** PR #29046's record 6570942095 ③ named this exact follow-up and its mechanical shape (`(param, names, lists)` twin at step 4; `package[` read at the door entry on both transports); the diff is that shape.
- `needs:contract-review` is not on the PR at the time of writing (labels: `documentation`, `size/m`, `tests`, `tooling`); nothing for this record to say about it. The PR is draft with no auto-merge armed. Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published contract on `main`: `GetMetaItemsRequestSchema` (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` 240) declares `packageId` as one optional string — the member `?package=` binds to through `metaItemPackageBinding` — and no `object` member at all; `?object=` is the view switcher's transport-level declaration (one object name) and `?package=` is #6877 / #22188's one-package scope (`all` or absence = every package); no spec text or docs page declares an array spelling of either, so the spec gives a bracketed key no meaning to take away. `@objectstack/client` builds `?package=` with `URLSearchParams.set` on every `/meta` read (`index.ts` 876, 1038, 1915, 1937) and sends no `object` on the list; the console (`ui/**`, read only) has no qs library and no bracketed `object` / `package` builder (the `'object[]'` literal in `app-shell/src/utils/paramValueShape.ts` is a value-shape name, not a query key); no docs or skill example spells either key bracketed. So no real producer loses a capability; this is the spec's own refusal class made real, the ruling line of #27484, #28548 and #29046 for a value that names nothing, not an implementation gap narrowed at the consumer.

Per `hits`-floor file: `meta-item-read-gate.ts` holds against the scenario (the two refusals are asked where each key is read, by both transports, and the shared builder reproduces the earlier literals); `meta-collection-routes.ts` and `meta-item-read-routes.ts` hold (the hand-off sits after the multiplicity gate and before the binding, in the door's own envelope dialect); the five test files pin each new answer on the transport that gives it plus the plain-spelling and absent controls, and nothing existing was edited to pass. Attempts to break it: a doubled bracketed key (one answer, ① item 3); a percent-encoded `package%5B%5D` (Hono decodes it before `queries()`); `packageId[`, `packages[`, `ID[` (unmatched, consistent with those plain spellings being other names or unread); a dispatcher-only host (same decision, pinned by the arity test and the census); the `_drafts` door (correctly not judged, ① item 2); a bracketed key on a write door (already an unknown name, ① item 6); a non-object query (early return). Nothing breaks.

The two-dialect note stands as it did on #28602 / #29046 (the chain's thrown refusal writes `RestServer`'s flat `{ error, code }`, the entry arity gate the nested one; status and `code` identical); it is pre-existing and not moved here.

Must-fix: none. Should-fix: ② — respell the declaration `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` (PR body and changeset) at the next head of this PR, if any; and file the `_drafts` `packageId[]` / `type[]` sibling as its own card.

**ACCEPT** · `domain:server` seat 2 · `os-steve` · `session_01ADHkmQxwoGb5fSnrFkpxmt` · 2026-11-02T11:46Z · head `1ee7e4f5` · claimed by seat 2 on #29199 (claim 6574465942, amendment on the card)

1. **Shape:** a draft against `main`, `!` title, `Fixes #29199`, BREAKING banner and one `adr-0087:` marker; `check-governed-merges --pr 29298`: NOT governed. No `packages/spec`, no `ui/**`.
